newsitem.title: UK: BBC boosts spending on global news coverage.
newsitem.headline: BBC boosts spending on global news coverage.

text.p: The BBC is to invest 15 million pounds ($25 million) as it reorganises and reinforces its foreign news operations, the corporation announced on Friday.
Its network of 42 overseas bureaux will be reorganised, seven of them upgraded to the status of regional "hubs" with full production support and state-of-the-art digital facilities.
These key bureaux will be in Brussels, Moscow, Hong Kong, Delhi, Johannesburg, Washington and Jerusalem.
The BBC plans to create posts for 30 new specialist journalists as it introduces more live coverage from around the world.
BBC News chief executive Tony Hall wants the state-owned corporation to remain a leading player in the global news market.
"I am determined that BBC News will stand head and shoulders above the competition when it comes to making sense of the complex world we live in," he said.
The funding will come from savings in production costs. The BBC said 60 percent of its journalists were now engaged in production but it wants to reverse this so the majority are out gathering news.
The BBC has some 2,000 foreign and domestic journalists, serving its national radio and television networks, radio's World Service and BBC World, its international television news service.
It is set to launch a 24-hour news channel when Britain introduces digital television in the next few months and also plans an Internet news service.
World Service, which has 143 million weekly listeners around the globe, is also considering a round-the-clock news service to complement its current output.($ = 0.592 British Pounds)
